title: UK Business Software AI Integration Database
selection_method: Editorial starter sample for UK business integration scoping; not a market-share survey, endorsement or exhaustive API catalogue.
evidence_policy: Vendor-documented capabilities are distinct from executed integration tests. Unknown values do not mean unavailable. AI use cases are Generativ editorial examples, not tested deployments.

systems.name: Airtable
systems.product_scope: Web API for base records and metadata; Enterprise admin functions are separate.

plans.minimum_plan: Free, Team, Business and Enterprise Scale
plans.notes: Core Web API is available on all plans. Monthly allowances: Free 1,000; Team 100,000; Business/Enterprise no monthly call cap, still rate limited.

webhooks.notes: Webhooks API notifies about changes to base records, fields and view membership. It is distinct from incoming automation webhooks.

authentication.notes: Token scopes and selected bases must match the user’s permissions. Legacy user API keys no longer work.

records.notes: Only bases/tables granted to the token; computed fields are not ordinary writable fields.

limitations.text: 5 requests/second per base on all pricing tiers; list responses are paginated at up to 100 records.

systems.ai_use_case: Categorise incoming requests and suggest values for an operations table.

systems.name: Asana
systems.product_scope: Tasks/projects REST API; premium resource features retain their plan requirements.

plans.minimum_plan: Free and paid accounts
plans.notes: Free accounts can use the API. Paid-only product features are not unlocked by having a developer token.

webhooks.notes: Task/project webhooks use an HTTPS receiver and handshake; events remain tied to the creating user/token’s access.

authentication.notes: PATs inherit user permissions. Use OAuth for apps acting for other users; view-only users have limited API access.

records.notes: Task CRUD is documented; access depends on project/workspace permissions.

limitations.text: 150 requests/minute on free domains; 1,500 on paid domains, per token. Search and concurrent operations have additional limits.

systems.ai_use_case: Extract proposed actions from an approved brief and create tasks after review.

systems.name: BambooHR
systems.product_scope: BambooHR employee API, including the cursor-paginated employee listing and employee update operation.

plans.minimum_plan: API-enabled account and authorised user; tier unconfirmed
plans.notes: The reviewed developer documents describe access and permissions, but do not establish a universal minimum paid subscription tier.

webhooks.notes: Global or permissioned webhooks notify employee changes. Permissioned subscriptions follow the creating user’s access. Custom fields are supported; custom tables are not supported by these webhooks.

authentication.notes: API keys act as the associated user: key as Basic username, an arbitrary password such as x. Developer apps can use scoped OAuth. List and write operations require their respective employee and field permissions.

records.notes: Employee listing, creation and update are documented. Some employment-history fields must be changed using their table endpoint instead of the employee update.

limitations.text: The employee listing defaults to 250 records and permits page[limit] up to 2,500; use opaque page[after]/page[before] cursors.
Unauthorised fields can be null and listed in _restrictedFields. Filtered or permission-limited totals are not a complete employee headcount.
Throttling can return 429; respect Retry-After rather than assuming a fixed universal request allowance.
The update endpoint can ignore an unknown field alias while returning success. Read back the intended fields; employment status history uses a separate table.

systems.ai_use_case: Build a permission-limited HR briefing and flag incomplete records for review, keeping restricted fields distinct from missing information.

api_contract.request_format: GET query parameters for lists; employee updates accept a field dictionary in JSON or XML.
api_contract.response_format: Employee listing is JSON with data, meta and _links. The list identifies restricted fields separately.
api_contract.pagination: page[limit] defaults to 250, maximum 2,500; opaque page[after]/page[before], with _links.next and _links.prev.

endpoints.request_shape: Optional fields list and page[limit]/cursor query parameters.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON data array, meta.total/meta.page and navigation links; employeeId is the internal ID.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON or XML dictionary of supported field aliases and values; only specified fields are changed.
endpoints.response_shape: 200 success; a successful status alone does not prove every supplied alias was recognised.

sources.title: List employees: fields, scopes and cursors

systems.name: BigChange
systems.product_scope: Modern REST API. Legacy JobWatch Web Services and DaaS are different products.

plans.minimum_plan: REST API licence; confirm contract
plans.notes: The usage policy says REST API access is priced on usage and refers to the customer’s licence details. A universal included subscription tier is not established.

webhooks.notes: Native outbound webhooks were not established from the REST reference and usage policy reviewed. Confirm supported event delivery with BigChange before promising real-time sync.

authentication.notes: Register an application, exchange client ID/secret for a bearer token, and send the customer-id header. Endpoint scopes are required.

records.notes: contacts:read and contacts:write govern the corresponding operations.
Uses contacts:persons:read/write scopes; consent operations are separately documented.

limitations.text: Requests can receive 429 and Retry-After; exact allowance is governed by the REST API licence. Reads can lag behind writes because the API is eventually consistent.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare a contact briefing for a field-service team from authorised customer records.

systems.name: Calendly
systems.product_scope: Calendly v2 scheduled-event retrieval and webhook subscriptions. Scheduling API booking operations are outside this entry.

plans.minimum_plan: Core API on all plans; webhook subscriptions require Standard, Teams or Enterprise
plans.notes: Calendly distinguishes ordinary API access from paid webhook eligibility. Enterprise-only endpoints have additional restrictions. Booking endpoints have separate conditions and are not assessed here.

webhooks.notes: Eligible paid plans can subscribe to invitee.created, invitee.canceled and routing_form_submission.created. Organisation-wide subscriptions depend on the caller’s role and scopes.

authentication.notes: Use a scoped Bearer token. Scheduled-event listing needs scheduled_events:read; organisation-wide access requires the appropriate administrator/owner role.

records.notes: This review covers retrieving events. Booking and cancellation endpoints exist but are not assessed as general event create/update operations.

limitations.text: The current default API limits are 500 requests per minute per user for paid plans and 50 for Free. Specific booking and OAuth endpoints have separate limits.
Scheduled-event lists have count default 20, maximum 100; use page_token and the response pagination metadata.
There is no general reschedule API endpoint. Calendly describes using the invitee’s reschedule URL instead.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare a meeting briefing from authorised event details and route cancellation notifications into the team’s existing workflow.

api_contract.request_format: GET query parameters with scoped Bearer authorisation.
api_contract.response_format: JSON collection array plus pagination for scheduled-event lists.
api_contract.pagination: count defaults to 20 and permits up to 100; page_token and pagination.next_page/next_page_token.

endpoints.request_shape: user, organization or group URI filters as permitted, plus count and page_token.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON collection of event objects and pagination navigation.

sources.title: API and plan frequently asked questions

systems.name: Capsule CRM
systems.product_scope: Capsule API v2; party records (people and organisations) and REST hooks.

plans.minimum_plan: Minimum commercial tier not established
plans.notes: The reviewed authentication and resource documents do not establish a universal minimum subscription plan. Confirm the target account’s entitlement.

webhooks.notes: REST hooks require a registered OAuth application and account administrator permissions; up to 20 subscriptions are supported.

authentication.notes: Send a Bearer token. Personal access tokens suit internal use; OAuth apps request read or read write access. A token does not bypass the user’s permissions.

records.notes: Party endpoints support listing, creation and updates; person and organisation fields differ.

limitations.text: The documented limit is 4,000 API requests per hour per user. Inspect X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset; 429 indicates throttling.
Collections use page/perPage and Link navigation; default perPage is 50 and the maximum is 100.
REST hooks cannot be inferred from personal-token API access: registered OAuth app and administrator conditions apply.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise a permitted customer record and propose structured contact updates for sales-team approval.

api_contract.request_format: JSON resource dictionaries inside a party wrapper for writes; query parameters for reads.
api_contract.response_format: Lists return a parties array; single-record responses use a party object.
api_contract.pagination: page and perPage (default 50, maximum 100); follow Link rel=next when present.

endpoints.request_shape: Optional page and perPage query parameters.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON object with a parties array.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON object with party containing the person or organisation fields and type.
endpoints.response_shape: Created party in the JSON party wrapper.

systems.name: ClickUp
systems.product_scope: Public API v2, plus separately documented v3 endpoints.

plans.minimum_plan: All ClickUp plans
plans.notes: Public API is available on all plans. User/guest management endpoints and some parameters require Enterprise or other higher tiers.

webhooks.notes: API-created subscriptions cover selected Workspace events and locations; webhook delivery follows the creating user’s access.

authentication.notes: Personal tokens for own use; OAuth for apps other people use. Both are permission constrained.

records.notes: Supported task fields; custom fields can require a separate endpoint.

limitations.text: Per-token requests/minute: Free Forever/Unlimited/Business 100; Business Plus 1,000; Enterprise/Enterprise Plus 10,000.
If the webhook’s creating user is disabled, it stops triggering. Verify signed events and handle duplicates.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft task descriptions and suggest due dates from approved client requests.

systems.name: Docusign
systems.product_scope: Docusign eSignature REST API v2.1: template-based envelopes, envelope updates and recipient status.

plans.minimum_plan: Production API eligibility and integration approval required
plans.notes: Developer/demo credentials do not establish production eligibility. Complete the applicable production integration approval and confirm the account’s API/Connect entitlements; a minimum commercial tier was not established.

webhooks.notes: Connect can send HTTPS POST notifications in XML or JSON. Account-, envelope-, recipient- and organisation-level configurations differ; confirm the account’s eligible configuration.

authentication.notes: Use OAuth Bearer access for an authorised account. Discover the production base URI through user info rather than substituting the demo host. JWT and authorisation-code setup have different consent requirements.

records.notes: Template creation and selected envelope updates are documented. Draft modifications, sending and voiding have different state requirements; envelope retrieval is not assessed here.
Read recipient status/routing and optionally tabs for a selected envelope; recipient write operations are outside this review.

limitations.text: Do not poll the status of the same envelope or API object more than once every 15 minutes. Connect callbacks reduce polling.
Envelope updates are state-dependent: draft modification and voiding an in-process envelope are distinct operations.
Demo and production environments have separate integration setup. Follow the current approval process before relying on production access.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise a signature request for approval and use authorised completion notifications to prepare the next onboarding task.

api_contract.request_format: JSON envelope definitions with OAuth Bearer authorisation; account and envelope IDs are path parameters.
api_contract.response_format: JSON envelope results and recipient status resources; Connect notification format is configured separately.
api_contract.pagination: The selected operations address one envelope or create one envelope; collection pagination is not assessed.

endpoints.purpose: Create an envelope from a template
endpoints.request_shape: JSON templateId, templateRoles and status; template role names must match. Sending changes state and can notify recipients.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON envelope summary, including envelopeId and status.

endpoints.request_shape: Account/envelope IDs in path; optional include_tabs query flag.

sources.title: Request a signature using a template

systems.name: ERPNext
systems.product_scope: ERPNext document access through Frappe REST API v1. Installed DocTypes and permissions vary by site; v2 methods are outside this entry.

plans.minimum_plan: An accessible ERPNext/Frappe site with authorised document access
plans.notes: Frappe documents resource APIs for DocTypes. The reviewed framework docs do not establish a hosting provider’s commercial plan entitlement or support allowance.

webhooks.notes: Configure a DocType, document event, condition and destination. Payloads can be JSON or form data. A webhook secret adds X-Frappe-Webhook-Signature, computed with HMAC-SHA256.

authentication.notes: Token authentication sends Authorization: token api_key:api_secret. Calls run with the associated user’s roles and permissions. OAuth Bearer access is also documented.

records.notes: Generic resource CRUD does not guarantee access to every installed DocType or unrestricted business-state transitions.

limitations.text: List responses default to 20 records and only the name field unless fields are requested. Specify filters and pagination rather than assuming a full dataset.
PUT updates supplied fields rather than replacing the whole document. Site-specific permissions and document validation still apply.
Webhooks apply only to configured DocTypes, events and conditions. They are not a complete stream of all database changes.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise permitted operational documents and prepare proposed changes that a user can approve before a document update.

api_contract.request_format: JSON document fields for POST and PUT; URL query parameters include JSON-encoded fields and filters.
api_contract.response_format: Successful resource responses wrap document objects or lists under data.
api_contract.pagination: limit_start and limit_page_length; default list length 20. Request fields explicitly.

endpoints.request_shape: fields and filters as JSON-encoded query parameters, plus limit_start/limit_page_length.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON object containing data: an array of permitted documents.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON dictionary of only the fields to change.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON object containing data: the resulting document.

systems.name: FreeAgent
systems.product_scope: Company API v2. Accountancy Practice API uses separate app access.

plans.minimum_plan: FreeAgent company account; exact commercial plan not confirmed
plans.notes: Official developer guidance requires a FreeAgent account and sufficient user access. It does not establish a separate minimum paid API tier in the pages reviewed.

webhooks.notes: No native outbound webhook facility was established in the reviewed company API documentation. Invoices support updated_since for polling; this is not proof that webhooks are unavailable.

authentication.notes: Register an app; obtain user consent and maintain access/refresh tokens. Resource access follows the authorised user’s access level.

records.notes: Requires the Estimates and Invoices access level; status-specific operations apply.

limitations.text: 120 requests/minute and 3,600/hour per user; 15 token refreshes/minute. Lists are paginated, with at most 100 items/page.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise overdue invoices and prepare follow-up drafts for review.

systems.name: Freshdesk
systems.product_scope: Freshdesk support API v2; not Freshsales or a blanket statement about Freshdesk Omni.

plans.minimum_plan: Growth, Pro or Enterprise for current API quotas
plans.notes: The current support table lists Free at 0 API calls; Growth 100/minute, Pro 400, Enterprise 700. Legacy accounts and trials can differ.

webhooks.notes: Ticket-update automation rules can call webhooks. Entitlement depends on the account generation and automation features; the reviewed guide lists Growth/Pro/Enterprise.

authentication.notes: Authenticate with the agent’s API key over HTTPS. The agent’s role determines allowed operations.

records.notes: Includes ticket updates, replies and notes; endpoint/role restrictions apply.
Contact operations are documented separately from ticket permissions.

limitations.text: Limits are account-wide, with additional endpoint caps; invalid requests also consume quota. Use the Freshdesk domain, not a custom CNAME.
Automation webhook callbacks have a documented 1,000/hour limit; excess requests are buffered.

systems.ai_use_case: Categorise a ticket and propose a priority and reply for a support agent.

systems.name: Google Workspace
systems.product_scope: Google Drive API as the documented example. Gmail, Calendar and Sheets have separate APIs and quotas.

plans.minimum_plan: Account with access to the relevant Google Drive files
plans.notes: Standard Drive API usage is currently available without an additional API charge. Workspace feature entitlements and administrator policies still apply; this entry does not establish access to every Workspace API.

webhooks.notes: Drive files/changes can send HTTPS push notifications. A notification signals a change; retrieve the current resource through the API.

authentication.notes: Scopes determine file access. Prefer drive.file for files explicitly used by the app; broader restricted scopes may require additional verification.

records.notes: File content/metadata operations depend on OAuth scope and the user’s file permissions.

limitations.text: Drive quotas changed for new projects from 1 May 2026; some existing projects retain earlier quotas. Check the project quota instead of assuming a universal request count.
Watch channels expire: up to 1 day for files and 1 week for changes; renew them.

systems.ai_use_case: Find approved project documents and draft an answer with links back to the originals.

systems.name: HubSpot
systems.product_scope: CRM APIs and app event subscriptions. Workflow webhook actions are a separate feature.

plans.minimum_plan: Free and paid tiers for core APIs
plans.notes: Free/Starter, Professional and Enterprise have documented private-app quotas. Access to a particular object or premium feature still depends on the account subscription and scopes.

webhooks.notes: Project-based apps can subscribe to CRM events. Service Keys do not support webhooks; use an app with webhook support.

authentication.notes: OAuth for distributed apps; scoped static credentials for a single account. Service Keys are described as public beta and require Developer Tools access.

records.notes: Core CRM contact properties; premium properties/features can have separate entitlements.

limitations.text: Private apps on Free/Starter: 100 requests/10 seconds per app and 250,000/day shared by the account. Search and other APIs have separate limits.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft a contact summary and propose CRM property updates after a meeting.

systems.name: Jira Cloud
systems.product_scope: Jira Cloud platform REST API v3. Jira Data Center is outside this entry.

plans.minimum_plan: Jira Cloud site; minimum paid edition not established
plans.notes: API access follows scopes, project permissions and app access policies. The reviewed references do not establish a separate minimum paid edition for core issue operations.

webhooks.notes: Issue/comment events can be delivered to webhook endpoints. REST-registered dynamic webhooks for OAuth apps expire after 30 days unless renewed.

authentication.notes: Use OAuth for third-party integrations. Personal scripts can use email plus an API token; access remains limited by the user’s permissions.

records.notes: Browse/Create/Edit permissions and field configuration constrain each operation; rich text uses Atlassian Document Format.

limitations.text: Since March 2026, Forge/Connect/OAuth apps use points-based and tiered quotas as well as burst/per-issue limits. API-token traffic retains existing burst limits.
OAuth apps can register 5 dynamic webhooks per app/user/tenant. Renew expiring registrations and implement supported event filters.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise a project issue and draft an update or new issue from approved support notes.

systems.name: Klaviyo
systems.product_scope: Server-side Profiles/Lists/Events APIs and system webhooks. Flow webhooks are distinct.

plans.minimum_plan: Account with API permissions; Advanced KDP/app partner for system webhooks
plans.notes: Core API key access is role/scope based. System Webhooks API is restricted to Advanced KDP customers and Klaviyo app partners; do not assume a normal email plan includes it.

webhooks.notes: System webhooks cover supported email/SMS/push/review/consent events. Flow webhooks are separately configured actions.

authentication.notes: Use scoped private keys or OAuth for server-side data. Public site IDs are only for the client-side API, not secure profile retrieval.

records.notes: Profile properties can be maintained through the API; subscriptions/consent use dedicated operations.

limitations.text: At most 10 system webhooks per account; activation can take up to 3 minutes. OAuth app webhooks are scoped to that app.

systems.ai_use_case: Enrich approved customer profile attributes for segmentation while preserving consent.

systems.name: Mailchimp
systems.product_scope: Marketing API v3. Transactional email is a separate product.

plans.minimum_plan: Mailchimp account; operation-specific plan entitlement
plans.notes: The developer overview requires an account but does not establish one minimum paid tier for all operations. Sending, automation and audience limits remain plan dependent.

webhooks.notes: Audience webhooks can notify about subscription/profile/email changes and campaign sending. Not every analytics event is an audience webhook.

authentication.notes: API keys for your own account; OAuth for integrations installed by third parties. Credentials are bounded by the authorising user’s role.

records.notes: Import/export and update audience members; subscription status must reflect actual consent.

limitations.text: Marketing API: 10 simultaneous connections per user and a 120-second timeout. Batch requests have additional queue limits.

systems.ai_use_case: Suggest audience tags from approved CRM attributes without changing marketing consent.

systems.name: Microsoft 365
systems.product_scope: Microsoft Graph: Outlook mail/calendar and SharePoint/OneDrive files. Other Graph products may have different licensing.

plans.minimum_plan: Licence for the underlying Microsoft 365 workload
plans.notes: There is no single plan entitlement covering every Graph API. Verify the Exchange, SharePoint or other workload licence and endpoint requirements for the tenant.

webhooks.notes: Graph change notifications support selected resources including Outlook messages/events and drive items; subscriptions expire and need renewal.

authentication.notes: Delegated access acts for a user; application permissions act without one and generally require admin consent. Request only the scopes for the workload.

records.notes: Calendars.ReadWrite permits event creation and changes; mailbox scope matters.
Mail.ReadWrite covers mailbox changes but does not itself permit sending; Mail.Send is separate.

limitations.text: Outlook supports at most 1,000 active subscriptions per mailbox across all apps. Shared-folder notifications require the appropriate application permission.
Handle subscription expiry and lifecycle events; do not assume a notification subscription is permanent.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft a meeting briefing from authorised calendar and mailbox content.

systems.name: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central
systems.product_scope: Business Central online standard API v2.0; customer resources. On-premises configuration is outside this entry.

plans.minimum_plan: Licensed Business Central environment with authorised API access
plans.notes: Confirm licence eligibility for the intended scenario. An Entra application also needs API permissions, tenant consent and Business Central object permission sets; the reviewed guide is not a commercial edition comparison.

webhooks.notes: Supported API resources can issue change notifications. Subscription creation and renewal require a validation handshake; subscriptions expire after three days unless renewed.

authentication.notes: For service-to-service access, register an Entra application, grant API.ReadWrite.All for business APIs and assign only the required Business Central permission sets. Request tokens with the Business Central .default scope.

records.notes: Standard customer resource operations. PATCH requires If-Match and retains omitted fields, although business rules can recalculate related values.

limitations.text: Online OData requests are limited per user to 6,000 in a five-minute sliding window and five concurrent executing requests; additional queue and environment limits also apply.
Customer PATCH requires If-Match; a stale ETag prevents the update.
Webhook delivery is delayed/coalesced and is not an immediate event for every individual field change. Renew subscriptions before their three-day expiry.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare a customer account briefing and propose contact-detail corrections, using ETags and approval before writing.

api_contract.request_format: JSON OData resource bodies; Bearer authorisation; If-Match on customer PATCH.
api_contract.response_format: Customer operations return JSON resource objects; OData collections use an envelope.
api_contract.pagination: Server-driven paging applies. Prefer: odata.maxpagesize can request a smaller page; online maximum is 20,000 entities.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON customer properties such as displayName and type, within the selected company.
JSON changed properties plus the required If-Match header.
endpoints.response_shape: 200 OK with the updated customer object.

systems.name: monday.com
systems.product_scope: Platform GraphQL API; API-created webhooks are separate from automation recipes.

plans.minimum_plan: Free, Basic, Standard, Pro and Enterprise
plans.notes: The platform API is documented as a free feature across plans. Daily allowances vary; individual product features may still be gated.

webhooks.notes: The create_webhook mutation subscribes to supported board/item events. The receiver must answer a verification challenge.

authentication.notes: Personal tokens mirror the user’s board, item and column permissions. App integrations can use OAuth tokens.

records.notes: Read/create items; update item column values using the appropriate column mutation and data format.

limitations.text: Daily calls: 1,000 on Free/Basic/Standard; 10,000 Pro; 25,000 Enterprise. Complexity, minute and concurrency budgets apply separately.

systems.ai_use_case: Classify an incoming work request and propose an item with status and owner.

systems.name: Notion
systems.product_scope: Notion public content API; administrative APIs have separate scope.

plans.minimum_plan: Free and paid workspaces
plans.notes: The API has quotas for all plans. Business/Enterprise receive higher connection limits; workspace content limits still apply.

webhooks.notes: Connections can receive page, database and other supported change events. Payloads identify changes; fetch content separately.

authentication.notes: Internal connections need pages shared with them; public connections use OAuth. PATs act with their creator’s workspace permissions.

records.notes: Content permissions and the selected API version govern operations; some computed properties are not writable. Page creation is outside this entry’s reviewed operation scope.

limitations.text: Per connection: 180 requests/minute on other plans and 600/minute on Business/Enterprise. A separate shared workspace budget and endpoint limits also apply.
Maximum request payload: 1,000 block elements and 500 KB; respect Retry-After on throttling.

systems.ai_use_case: Turn approved meeting notes into draft project pages and action lists.

systems.name: Odoo
systems.product_scope: Odoo 19 JSON-2 external API and Studio automation; hosted commercial plan requirements. Earlier RPC APIs and Community hosting are not assessed.

plans.minimum_plan: Custom plan for hosted external API access
plans.notes: Odoo documents external API availability on Custom, excluding One App Free and Standard. This is not a claim about separately managed Community deployments.

webhooks.notes: Studio automation rules can send a webhook notification to a URL with selected record fields. This needs a configured automation action; it is not an automatic event feed for every model.

authentication.notes: Use a dedicated user API key with only the necessary access rights. X-Odoo-Database selects the database when needed; model and record access rules still apply.

records.notes: search_read, create and write are model methods; fields and access rights depend on the database.

limitations.text: JSON-2 is new in Odoo 19. Model methods and fields depend on the database; inspect its /doc reference rather than assuming another installation has identical models.
Each JSON-2 call runs in its own transaction. Multiple calls do not form one atomic transaction.
Automation webhook fields and trigger conditions must be configured explicitly; review the selected payload before enabling the rule.

systems.ai_use_case: Produce a contact briefing from permitted partner fields and send proposed record corrections for approval.

api_contract.request_format: All model calls use POST with a JSON dictionary of named method arguments, including ids/context where applicable.
api_contract.response_format: The JSON-serialised method result is returned directly; errors use an error object with HTTP 4xx/5xx status.
api_contract.pagination: For search_read, use the ORM domain, fields, offset and limit arguments. This is model pagination, not a REST next-page URL.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON dictionary with domain filters and fields; optional offset and limit.
endpoints.response_shape: Array of selected contact records, including record IDs.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON dictionary containing ids and vals; access rules apply to every target record.
endpoints.response_shape: Boolean success result from the ORM write method.

sources.title: ORM search, create and write methods

systems.name: Pipedrive
systems.product_scope: Core CRM API and Webhooks v2.

plans.minimum_plan: Lite, Growth, Premium and Ultimate
plans.notes: API access is available to account users by default, but admins can restrict personal API-token access. Plan/seat counts set the token budget.

webhooks.notes: Create/change/delete subscriptions for supported CRM objects. Webhook delivery respects the associated user’s permissions.

authentication.notes: OAuth is required for Marketplace apps. Personal API tokens use the user’s account permissions.

records.notes: Use the current Deals endpoints and required fields.

limitations.text: Burst limits vary by plan and authentication type; Lite personal tokens allow 20 requests/2 seconds. Daily token budgets count endpoint costs, not just HTTP requests.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise a deal and suggest a next action based on approved CRM information.

systems.name: QuickBooks Online
systems.product_scope: QuickBooks Online Accounting REST API. Desktop and Self-Employed are outside this entry.

plans.minimum_plan: QuickBooks Online company plus Intuit app access; minimum UK plan unconfirmed
plans.notes: The reviewed developer pages establish company authorisation and developer-tier quotas, but not a universal minimum UK business subscription. Check the feature entitlement in the target company.

webhooks.notes: Entity-change webhooks include invoices and customers. Production and sandbox subscriptions are configured separately and require the company to authorise the app.

authentication.notes: Connect each company through OAuth. Validate incoming webhook signatures with the app-specific verifier token.

records.notes: Updates require the current SyncToken. Required customer and line fields, locale and company preferences matter.

limitations.text: 500 requests/minute per realm and 10/second per realm and app. Builder has 500,000 included CorePlus calls per workspace/month; higher usage depends on the developer programme.
Progress invoicing is not supported by the invoice API. Do not treat every UI feature as an API capability.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise invoice status and prepare proposed line descriptions for an accountant to approve.

systems.name: Sage Accounting
systems.product_scope: Sage Business Cloud Accounting API v3.1 for UK businesses. Sage 50 and Sage Intacct are separate products.

plans.minimum_plan: Accounting Start for sales invoices; Standard/Plus for more features
plans.notes: Sage documents API differences between Start, Standard and Plus. Purchase invoice and product writes require the relevant higher-tier feature; inventory and multicurrency are Plus features.

webhooks.notes: Native outbound webhooks were not established in the reviewed Accounting guides. Confirm event delivery before designing real-time synchronisation.

authentication.notes: A user grants readonly or full_access. Use X-Business to select the business; otherwise the lead business is used.

records.notes: Draft/pro forma release and payment allocation use separate operations; invoice state limits changes.

limitations.text: Access tokens last 5 minutes; refresh tokens last 31 days and must be rotated from the refresh response.
A draft does not post to the accounts. Marking an invoice paid requires a payment/allocation, not a direct status update.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare draft sales invoices from approved work records, with accounting review before release.

systems.name: Salesforce
systems.product_scope: Salesforce REST API and Change Data Capture; not a guarantee for every Salesforce product.

plans.minimum_plan: Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance; Professional with API add-on
plans.notes: Developer Edition also includes API access for development. The organisation and the user must both have API access enabled. Confirm entitlements on newer or negotiated editions.

webhooks.notes: Change Data Capture publishes create/update/delete/undelete events through a subscription stream. This is an event-stream option, not a generic outbound HTTP webhook.

authentication.notes: An authorised app and user permissions govern access; object and field permissions still apply.

records.notes: Only objects/fields exposed to the authorised user; check the specific object’s supported operations.

limitations.text: CDC is documented for Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer editions. Event delivery allocations and API request allowances must be checked for the organisation.

systems.ai_use_case: Create a reviewable opportunity summary from the account and its recent activity.

systems.name: ServiceM8
systems.product_scope: ServiceM8 API 1.0; selected job operations and object webhooks.

plans.minimum_plan: Minimum subscription tier not established
plans.notes: Authentication documentation establishes account/app setup, but not a universal minimum commercial plan. Confirm the customer account entitlement and any usage charges.

webhooks.notes: Object notifications identify the object UUID and changed fields, with a resource URL to retrieve the record. OAuth subscriptions require a challenge response; API-key subscriptions do not.

authentication.notes: Private integrations can use X-API-Key. Public integrations use OAuth 2.0 and partner registration. Job permissions distinguish read_jobs, create_jobs and manage_jobs.

records.notes: Create and update use POST; update is addressed by job UUID. Required permissions and fields remain endpoint-specific.

limitations.text: Cursor pages contain up to 1,000 records; start with cursor=-1 and follow the x-next-cursor response header until absent.
Object callbacks are change notifications, not a complete job snapshot. Fetch the linked resource before using the updated fields.
API access can trigger account charges for some operations. A successful authentication does not establish commercial entitlement.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft a job summary for a dispatcher from authorised job records, then submit approved corrections through the job update endpoint.

api_contract.request_format: GET query parameters; POST field payloads follow the selected endpoint reference.
api_contract.response_format: JSON resource arrays for list calls; write results must be interpreted using the endpoint response and headers.
api_contract.pagination: cursor=-1; follow x-next-cursor, up to 1,000 records per page.

endpoints.request_shape: Optional $filter and cursor query parameters; no request body.
endpoints.response_shape: Array of job objects; pagination cursor is returned in x-next-cursor.

endpoints.request_shape: Job fields to update in the request body, addressed by UUID; consult the reference for accepted fields and encoding.
endpoints.response_shape: 200 success; do not assume the response contains a complete updated job.

systems.name: Shopify
systems.product_scope: GraphQL Admin API. Storefront API is a separate surface.

plans.minimum_plan: Shopify store with an installed, authorised app
plans.notes: Standard plans have a GraphQL Admin quota; Advanced/Plus/enterprise have higher quotas. Access to protected customer fields and specialised APIs has separate requirements.

webhooks.notes: App event subscriptions can deliver order/product and other supported topics over HTTPS. Scopes and protected-data approval affect payloads.

authentication.notes: An installed app uses an Admin API access token and approved access scopes. Custom app creation/distribution rules must also be checked.

records.notes: GraphQL product queries and mutations; variant operations and permissions are separate.

limitations.text: GraphQL Admin restore rates: Standard 100 cost points/second; Advanced 200; Plus 1,000. A single query may not exceed 1,000 points.
Unapproved protected customer fields can be redacted; API access alone does not establish permission to retrieve personal data.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft product descriptions from approved product data for a merchandiser to review.

systems.name: Simpro
systems.product_scope: Simpro build-specific REST API v1.0; selected job operations.

plans.minimum_plan: Customer build and application registration required; tier unconfirmed
plans.notes: The reviewed API documents describe build access and app registration, but do not establish a minimum commercial subscription tier.

webhooks.notes: An administrator can configure event subscriptions. JSON callbacks carry an action and reference IDs for a subsequent API lookup; verify X-Response-Signature with the configured secret.

authentication.notes: OAuth grants include authorisation code and client credentials. API keys provide persistent access; select a grant appropriate to user-specific or system-wide access and register with the customer build.

records.notes: GET lists/retrieves jobs, POST creates and PATCH updates selected fields within a company.

limitations.text: More than 10 requests per second from an integration to a single client build triggers HTTP 429 until traffic falls below the limit.
Lists default to 30 records; pageSize can increase this to 250. Multi-company builds require the correct company ID.
Job PATCH returns 204 without a resource body. Validation errors and fields allowed for creation versus update differ.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare a service-job briefing from the job record, then route proposed changes to an operator for approval.

api_contract.request_format: JSON bodies for POST/PATCH; page and pageSize query parameters for lists.
api_contract.response_format: Lists are JSON arrays; individual resources are objects. Successful job PATCH has no response body.
api_contract.pagination: page is the page number; pageSize defaults to 30 and allows up to 250. Inspect Result-Total, Result-Pages and Result-Count headers.

endpoints.request_shape: Company ID in path; optional page/pageSize query parameters.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON array with job ID, Description and Total fields in the default listing.

endpoints.request_shape: JSON object containing supported job fields to change.
endpoints.response_shape: 204 No Content on success; invalid input can return 422.

sources.title: Pagination, company scope and error formats

systems.name: Slack
systems.product_scope: Web API and outbound Events API. Incoming webhooks only post into Slack.

plans.minimum_plan: Free and paid workspaces, subject to app permissions and retention
plans.notes: API rate tiers apply across Slack plans. Available message history and app installation controls still depend on the workspace.

webhooks.notes: Events API delivers authorised events to an HTTP endpoint or Socket Mode. Incoming webhooks are a different, write-into-Slack feature.

authentication.notes: Scopes and channel membership limit visibility. An app cannot read every private channel merely because it is installed.

records.notes: History needs the appropriate history scope. Posting/editing requires chat scopes and editing rights for the message.

limitations.text: New commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps have stricter history/replies limits; internal customer-built apps keep the documented Tier 3 history limit.
Events API limit: 30,000 deliveries per workspace, app and hour.

systems.ai_use_case: Summarise an opted-in project channel and post a reviewable weekly update.

systems.name: Stripe
systems.product_scope: Stripe v1 Customer API and event webhooks. Payment execution and v2 API contracts are outside this review.

plans.minimum_plan: Stripe account with appropriate server-side API access
plans.notes: The reviewed key documentation establishes account access and key permissions, not a universal pricing plan. Product eligibility, live activation and transaction charges need separate confirmation.

webhooks.notes: Stripe sends signed HTTPS event callbacks. Verify Stripe-Signature against the original request body and the endpoint secret. Event formats and API versions require explicit handling.

authentication.notes: Use a server-side secret or restricted key with the required resource permissions. Publishable keys do not provide equivalent server access. Test/sandbox and live credentials are separate.

records.notes: Customer reads and POST create/update are documented; this does not establish payment, billing or refund capabilities.

limitations.text: Default global limits are 100 operations per second in live mode and 25 in sandbox; endpoints generally default to 25 requests per second, with documented exceptions and additional concurrency limits.
429 responses may reflect different limiters. Inspect Stripe-Rate-Limited-Reason and back off rather than treating every 429 as the same quota.
v1 cursor pagination uses starting_after or ending_before; limit is 1–100, default 10. These rules do not describe Stripe v2 pagination.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare a customer account summary and propose approved metadata updates without initiating a charge.

api_contract.version: v1 Customers; account/request API version also applies
api_contract.request_format: Form-encoded parameters for the selected v1 POST endpoint; query parameters for lists.
api_contract.response_format: Customer objects are JSON. List responses use object=list with data, has_more and url.
api_contract.pagination: starting_after or ending_before cursor; limit 1–100, default 10; inspect has_more.

endpoints.request_shape: Optional limit and cursor query parameters.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON list envelope with data containing Customer objects and has_more.

endpoints.request_shape: Form-encoded customer parameters such as name, email and metadata.
endpoints.response_shape: JSON Customer object with its id.

systems.name: Trello
systems.product_scope: Trello REST API; not Atlassian Jira APIs.

plans.minimum_plan: Trello account; minimum paid tier not established
plans.notes: The reviewed developer pages describe API-key/token access without establishing a minimum paid subscription. Board features and permissions still apply.

webhooks.notes: Model-change webhooks are bound to a token and can observe only models it can access.

authentication.notes: Use authorisation for the relevant user and boards. Current webhook documentation also describes OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens.

records.notes: Read/create/update cards within authorised boards.

limitations.text: 300 requests/10 seconds per API key and 100/10 seconds per token. The members endpoint has an additional limit.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft task cards and labels from approved project notes.

systems.name: WooCommerce
systems.product_scope: Self-hosted WooCommerce REST API v3; Store API has different access and limits.

plans.minimum_plan: Core WooCommerce; no separate API subscription
plans.notes: The REST API is part of WooCommerce. A working WordPress/WooCommerce site and hosting are required; extensions may add their own paid features.

webhooks.notes: Core webhooks cover order, product, customer and coupon events. Manage them in Advanced settings or the API.

authentication.notes: Use HTTPS and a key with read, write or read/write permission. Access follows the associated WordPress user’s capabilities.

records.notes: REST resource operations and user permissions apply.
Core product resource; extension-specific metadata may need separate handling.

limitations.text: Requires compatible WordPress/WooCommerce versions and non-default permalinks. Host configuration can affect auth headers and allowed HTTP methods.
Webhook delivery can fail or be disabled after repeated failures; monitor deliveries and verify the signature.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare product-copy changes or a customer-service order summary for approval.

systems.name: Xero
systems.product_scope: Accounting API; UK business organisation. Payroll and Practice Manager are outside this entry.

plans.minimum_plan: Xero organisation + developer tier
plans.notes: Developer Starter supports up to 5 connections. A sixth requires Core. These developer tiers are separate from the business accounting subscription; confirm the organisation supports the intended feature.

webhooks.notes: App webhooks cover selected events, including contact and invoice creation/updates; not every Accounting API object.

authentication.notes: Use an authorised Xero organisation and the necessary accounting scopes. Request offline_access for ongoing webhook access beyond the initial token lifetime.

records.notes: Write permissions and invoice status affect which changes are allowed.

limitations.text: Current developer FAQ: 1,000 calls/day per organisation on Starter; 5,000 on higher tiers. Also 60/minute and 5 concurrent calls per connection. Older limits FAQs still show 5,000 without the Starter distinction.
Journals and Practice Manager require Advanced tier plus approval; they are not implied by basic Accounting API access.

systems.ai_use_case: Prepare draft invoice descriptions from approved job notes, with a person checking the invoice before issue.

systems.name: Zendesk
systems.product_scope: Zendesk Support API and webhooks; Chat and other products have separate limits.

plans.minimum_plan: Support Team and higher; Suite quotas vary
plans.notes: Support Team API quota is documented. Suite plan allowances differ from standalone Support; check which product the account uses.

webhooks.notes: Support events and ticket triggers can send HTTP requests to configured endpoints; a webhook is not a subscription to every possible field change.

authentication.notes: OAuth access tokens are supported. Zendesk says all API tokens stop working on 30 April 2027; use OAuth for new builds.

records.notes: Ticket properties/comments subject to role, field and endpoint restrictions.

limitations.text: Support Team: 200 requests/minute; Professional 400; Enterprise 700. Some endpoints have stricter limits.
Trial accounts: at most 10 webhooks and 60 invocations/minute.

systems.ai_use_case: Draft a support reply using the ticket and approved help content, ready for agent review.

systems.name: Zoho CRM
systems.product_scope: Zoho CRM API v8; workflow webhooks and API notifications are distinct mechanisms.

plans.minimum_plan: Free and paid editions for core API
plans.notes: Free has an API credit allowance. Workflow webhook actions are documented for Professional and higher; do not infer their availability from core API access.

webhooks.notes: Outbound workflow webhooks require the applicable workflow entitlement. Check the separate Notifications API for supported record-change subscriptions.

authentication.notes: Use a token with module/action scopes and the appropriate data-centre API domain. User permissions still apply.

records.notes: Examples include leads, contacts and deals; the module and field must support the requested operation.

limitations.text: Free: 5,000 API credits in a rolling 24 hours and 5 concurrent calls. Paid credits/concurrency vary by edition. Insert/update/upsert requests allow up to 100 records.

systems.ai_use_case: Classify an enquiry, propose a lead record and route it to the right sales team.
